meaning: The B2B SaaS AI Visibility Benchmark 2026 by Citant.ai, dataset v1.5 (2026-11-07). License CC BY 4.0. v1.5 changes results-aggregate, overlap-per-prompt, summary-metrics, cited-domains and adjudication and adds own-domains, source-domains, chatgpt-funnel-per-question, tracker-domains and chatgpt-prompts-as-sent; queries, claude-perplexity-recount, tracker-per-engine and tracker-hand-reads are unchanged and keep their names. verify_benchmark.py in the repository recomputes the main numbers from these files and lists what it cannot check. Report: https://citant.ai/research/b2b-saas-ai-visibility-benchmark-2026/
Question id P01 to P50, 10 per category, frozen before collection.
G2 category the question belongs to.
Question exactly as pasted into each platform.
One brand per category: 94 rows, 93 companies (HubSpot is tracked in Sales Engagement and Help Desk).
Registrable host of the brand's site, lowercase, without www.
Leader, Challenger or Small: listing-position label from the September 2-3 sampling sheet. Not company size and not G2 Grid placement.
Vendor's total G2 review count recorded September 2 to 3, 2026.
Of the category's 10 questions, how many ChatGPT answers (web search on, single run, September 4 2026) named the brand. Whole-word name, alias or domain match; common-word names hand-read.

Same, Claude, single manual run, September 3-4 2026. v1.4: recounted on the answer text only, each match checked in its sentence, common-word names and table cells that the transcript copy glued to the next word read by hand; a brand that appears only in a source card or a citation link is not counted (see claude-perplexity-recount).

Same, Perplexity, single manual run, September 8 2026. v1.4: recounted on the answer text only, each match checked in its sentence, common-word names and table cells that the transcript copy glued to the next word read by hand; a brand that appears only in a source card or a citation link is not counted (see claude-perplexity-recount).
Of the 10 questions, how many times a brand-owned domain (see own-domains) appeared in ChatGPT's search results for that question, final attempt only. Per-question rows: chatgpt-funnel-per-question.

Of the 10 questions, how many times a brand-owned domain (see own-domains) was cited in the text of ChatGPT's final answer. v1.5: image carousels and thumbnails no longer count as citations (see chatgpt-funnel-per-question, own_site_image_only). A count can exceed retrieved: on 3 pairs the answer cited a brand site that was not in that question's search results.
AI Access Score 0-100 from Citant's AI Crawler Access Report on the corrected September 26 rescan; blank = site could not be scored. Used in the report.
Same, original September 5 scan, before a scanner correction (identity-verifying firewalls had been read as blocks). Kept for transparency.
yes = brand name is a common word; bare-word mentions were read by hand and counted only where they refer to the company.
yes = the hand read changed at least one named count in v1.1 (see adjudication file).

Share of tracked chats in the brand's OWN category that mention it, ChatGPT + Google Gemini + Google AI Overviews combined, September 7 2026 sample (0-1). v1.2 divided by all chats of a two-category tracking project (about 2x too low for Project Management, Sales Engagement, Help Desk and Core HR). Text matching runs high for common-word names.
Tracker chats mentioning the brand in its own category across every run held, September 7-14 2026, after hand reads (see tracker-hand-reads). Zero here is the tracker half of the five-platform test.
How to read the two tracker columns.
yes = named on none of its 10 questions by ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity.

yes = named by none of the 3 manual engines AND zero tracker mentions in the brand's own category across every tracker run held (September 7-14 2026, Gemini, AI Overviews and repeated ChatGPT; common-word hits read by hand). The report's headline (32 of 94 in v1.4, 30 of 94 in v1.3). v1.3 changed its members: Smartsheet and Lusha were named in category on Sept 8-14 and leave; SAP (its only hit was a Core HR answer) and Backlog (common-word hits only) join. v1.4 adds Native Teams and morningmate: their only Perplexity hit was a source card or citation link.
One per question. Consulted = domains that surfaced while each engine researched (ChatGPT search results; Claude and Perplexity source lists).
no = Claude answered this question without listing any web source; it counts as consulting zero domains (7 of 50 questions).
Jaccard similarity of registrable domains between engines for that question.
Distinct registrable domains consulted by any engine on that question.

Of union_domains, how many were consulted by exactly one, exactly two, or all three engines on that question. Per-question counts: on the 7 questions where Claude listed no source, no domain can be on all three, so on_all_present and jaccard_all_present are 0 and a domain ChatGPT and Perplexity share counts in on_exactly_two. The report's 917 / 655 / 187 / 75 are distinct domains across all 50 questions and all three engines, so these columns do not sum to them; recompute them from source-domains (layer consulted).
Page-level (host + path) counts and Jaccard where both engines carried page URLs; blank where not available.
Every aggregate in the report as num / den, with engine, layer and category.

Classes: own vendor = a domain in own-domains; review UGC = g2.com, capterra.com, reddit.com, youtube.com, trustradius.com; editorial = forbes.com, techrepublic.com; institutional = .org/.edu; all other domains = everything else (untracked vendors, blogs, directories, listicles, other publishers; the class value in the files is other). Unit: distinct question-domain incidences on registrable domains. v1.5: the cited rows count text citations only, 227 incidences; the 24 image-only incidences are reported apart.

Every registrable domain ChatGPT surfaced per category, in three layers: cited (text citations, 149 rows), image_only (carousels and thumbnails only, 22 rows) and consulted (search results, 630 rows). All classes, no cap, no filter. questions = how many of the category's of_questions questions; question_ids lists them. Claude and Perplexity source lists are in source-domains. v1.5 replaces the v1.3 file, which capped each category at 25 rows, excluded tracked vendors and listed hosts unmerged.

Repeated-run figures from the tracking platform, one row per brand x own category x engine (ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overview), all 94 brand entries. Sample: September 7 2026, 3 runs of each question per engine (about 30 chats per engine per category). Chats where the platform stored no answer are excluded (AI Overviews keeps 18 of 30 in Help Desk, 28 in Core HR and 29 in Sales Engagement; every other cell keeps 30).
Tracked chats with an answer for that category and engine on September 7 (the denominator).
Of those chats, how many mention the brand (the numerator).
chats_mentioning_brand / chats_in_category (0-1).
Average list position of the brand in the chats that mention it.

Platform sentiment score 0-100 for that engine, computed by the platform at project level over the brand's mentions; blank where the project was exported blended across engines or the brand had no mentions. Noisy for brands with few mentions.
One row per tracker chat whose brand hit was read by hand and excluded (brand, category, date, engine, chat id, decision).

One per common-word brand and engine. hand_read_before and hand_read_after are the v1.1 hand read as logged in v1.2; hand_read_question_ids are the questions counted after it; hand_read_changed = yes where the read moved the count. current_named_questions and current_question_ids are the count in force today; current_count_from says which version set it (Claude and Perplexity were recounted in v1.4). v1.4 had overwritten the before and after columns with the recount; v1.5 restores them and keeps the recount beside them.

One row per brand entry x engine (Claude, Perplexity): named question count in v1.3 and v1.4 and the v1.4 question ids. v1.4 counts a brand only where its name, domain or alias is in the answer text; source cards, citation links and the pasted question do not count; common-word names read by hand.
Registrable domains ChatGPT cited in the answer text on that question (v1.5: text citations only).
Registrable domains that appeared only in an image carousel or thumbnail on that question. New in v1.5.
New in v1.5: every domain counted as a tracked brand's own, one row per brand entry and domain. basis says where it came from; added_in says which version added it.

New in v1.5: one row per question, engine, layer and registrable domain, with its class. Layers: chatgpt consulted 1,161 rows, cited 227, image_only 24; claude consulted 333; perplexity consulted 664. Consulted for ChatGPT means the domains in its search results on the final attempt; for Claude and Perplexity, their expanded source lists. Consulted means surfaced, not read: the exports do not show which pages a model opened. The base file for the report's overlap, source-mix, Reddit and YouTube figures.

New in v1.5: one row per brand entry and question, 940 rows, the per-question base of the report's ChatGPT funnel. own_site_retrieved and own_site_cited use the definitions in results-aggregate; own_site_image_only marks a brand domain that appeared only in an image carousel or thumbnail.
The brand entry and the engine the hand read applies to.
Named-question count before and after the v1.1 hand read.
Questions counted after the hand read; yes where the read moved the count.
The count in force today, its questions, and the version that set it.
The brand entry and one domain counted as its own.
website = the brand's listed site; alias = another domain the brand owns. added_in = the dataset version that added it.

column: query_id / category / engine / layer / domain / class
meaning: Question id, category, engine, layer (consulted, cited, image_only), registrable domain, and class (own_vendor, review_ugc, editorial, institutional, other).
The brand entry and one of its category's 10 questions.
1 or 0 for that pair: named in the answer, a brand domain in the search results, a brand domain cited in the text, a brand domain only in an image carousel or thumbnail.

New in v1.5: the wording ChatGPT received, beside the wording in queries.csv. All 50 ChatGPT prompts carried the year at the end; Claude and Perplexity received the questions as listed in queries.csv. Non-breaking spaces and surrounding whitespace are removed; P48 was sent with no space before the year.
Question id, category, and the wording in queries.csv.

The prompt in the final attempt; how many attempts the chat holds; the first attempt's text where there were two (P12 and P16, first sent without the year and then edited in the same chat). Counts use the final attempt only.
Category, engine (chatgpt), layer (cited, image_only, consulted), registrable domain, and class as in source-domains.
How many of the category's questions the domain appeared on, the number of questions, and their ids.

column: project / categories / domain / class / retrieved_chats / retrievals / citations / citation_rate
meaning: Tracker project (A, B, C), its G2 categories, the domain, the platform's own class label, tracked chats that retrieved the domain, times retrieved, times cited, and the platform's average rate.
Cited layer only. primary = a grouped citation in the answer; supporting = a supporting link in such a group; plain_link = a link ChatGPT wrote into the answer text itself.
The brand entry and its G2 category.
Question id, category, and the wording in queries.csv.
Registrable domains each engine consulted on that question (the rows of source-domains, layer consulted).
The domains on all three engines for that question (empty on the 7 questions where Claude listed no source).

column: metric / engine / layer / category / num / den / rate / note
meaning: The metric, where it was measured, numerator, denominator, rate (num / den), and a note.
The brand entry, the tracked engine, and whether the brand name is also a common word.

column: brand / category / date / engine / chat_id / decision
meaning: The brand entry, the tracked chat read by hand, and the decision on it.

column: brand / category / engine / named_questions_v1_3 / named_questions_v1_4 / named_question_ids_v1_4 / changed
meaning: The brand entry and engine, named counts in v1.3 and v1.4, the v1.4 question ids, and whether the recount moved the count.

Three-way Jaccard for the question. It is 0 on the 7 questions where Claude listed no source (P10, P20, P30, P40, P41, P45, P50); the report's 0.021 includes them as zero and its 0.024 is the 43 others.

New in v1.5: the rows of the third-party tracker's source exports that the report quotes. retrieved_chats = tracked chats that retrieved the domain; retrievals = times retrieved; citations = times cited; citation_rate = the platform's average, which can exceed 1 and is not a percentage. categories = the G2 categories the project covers. class = the platform's own label (Competitor, UGC, Reference, Corporate, You, Institutional), not the report's source classes.
